description: We are a multidisciplinary powerhouse team of students from King Abdulaziz University (KAU), bringing together a dynamic mix of graduating seniors and current students. Our expertise spans across Microbiology, Management Information Systems (MIS), Software Programming.
summary:
We created BASIRA, an interactive, simulation-based disaster-resilient planning game powered by NASA’s advanced NISAR radar data.

 The project tackles the severe seasonal floods and cholera outbreaks around Uganda’s Lake Kyoga. It places players in charge of a vulnerable village on a tight budget, requiring them to strategically allocate resources—such as digging new wells, repairing broken pumps, installing solar lighting, and raising pathways. Players then test their strategies against actual 2026 flood simulations driven by all-weather NISAR radar observations. If the strategy fails, the village floods; if successful, the design automatically converts into an actionable GIS map for local councils to deploy before the next rains.

BASIRA bridges the gap between complex Earth observation telemetry and grassroots community preparedness, transforming sophisticated satellite data into a practical, life-saving tool for real-world climate resilience.
details:
• BASIRA is an interactive web-based simulation game and decision-support tool designed to help plan safe water points and infrastructure in flood-prone regions, specifically demonstrated around Lake Kyoga in Uganda.


• How it works: Players or planners act to build wells, pumps, and solar water points on safe, elevated ground where historical satellite radar data shows no flooding. Then, the system replays the actual 2026 wet season using real NASA-ISRO NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) radar passes (covering 34 passes from June to October 2026) to test whether the chosen locations survive the floods or get submerged. If a well is flooded, planners must adjust locations based on radar evidence before submitting the final plan to district water offices.


• What benefits does it have?
• Securing Clean Water: Prevents wells and hand pumps from being drowned by seasonal lake rises, protecting communities from waterborne diseases and contaminated floodwater.
• Cost & Resource Efficiency: Prevents wasting funds on rebuilding wells in the exact same vulnerable spots year after year.
• Accessibility: Free to play on any phone or laptop via a web browser with zero installation or login required, making it accessible for schools, NGOs, and local planners.


• What is the intended impact of the project?
• Empowering Local Authorities: Providing district water offices and aid organizations with practical, radar-backed site reports to make data-driven infrastructure decisions.
• Protecting Vulnerable Communities: Safeguarding thousands of households and villages (such as the 8 modeled villages around Lake Kyoga impacting over 1.25 million people across 13 districts) from losing access to safe drinking water during extreme weather events.
• Educational Outreach: Raising climate and space-tech awareness by letting students and citizens learn about satellite data and disaster resilience through gamified problem-solving.


• What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
• Languages & Core Technologies: TypeScript, Three.js (for 3D hexagonal mapping and visualization), and DuckDB for spatial data processing.
• Data Sources: NASA Earthdata Search, ﻿﻿ASF Vertex (NASA’s radar archive), NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar (via ASF DAAC), MODIS Terra true color (via NASA GIBS), WorldPop (for population data), WPDx (Water Point Data Exchange), OpenStreetMap, and Overture Maps.
• Integration & Export Tools: Built to export site plans and reports compatible with QGIS, ArcGIS, and Google Earth.
• Development Assistance: Developed using modern AI coding tools.


• How is your project creative?
• Gamification of Earth Observation: It transforms complex, technical satellite radar data (which usually requires specialized GIS software) into an engaging, interactive strategy game ("Save the village") led by an AI guide character named Orbi.
• Overcoming Cloud Obstacles: Traditional optical satellites are blinded by thick monsoon clouds during rainy seasons; BASIRA creatively leverages synthetic aperture radar (SAR) which penetrates clouds to reveal hidden floodwaters with high precision.
• Actionable Gamification: It bridges the gap between gaming and real-world humanitarian aid by turning a successful game-level completion into a verifiable site report ready for real district water offices.


• What factors did your team consider?
• Data Accuracy & Realism: Using real geographical parameters, 1,125 village service areas, actual 2026 satellite passes, and elevation refinement (30-meter elevation data) rather than fictional scenarios.
• User Experience & Accessibility: Ensuring the platform runs smoothly on any web browser or mobile phone without requiring heavy installations, logins, or paid software.
• Scalability & Sustainability: Designing a sustainable model that serves schools for free while offering low-cost customized planners ($2,000/area/year) and open-source flexibility for global expansion to other flood-prone regions worldwide.
